title: Crash recovery: after an unexpected stop, a ticked list brings the open terminals back
story: After Maestro crashes, is killed or loses power, the next start shows a 'Maestro stopped unexpectedly' dialog listing the terminals that were open. Ticked ones come back: Claude terminals continue their conversation, shells reopen empty with an amber warning, parked ones return to the shelf, and a missing folder shows greyed. A normal close never shows the dialog; on macOS the menu's Quit now asks the same quit question as the close button.

checks.criterion: After a kill, the dialog lists exactly the open terminals
checks.steps: Open project 'demo-app' with two Claude terminals ('alpha', 'beta') and one plain shell, kill Maestro in Task Manager, start it again.
checks.expected: 'Maestro stopped unexpectedly' with day and time, all three rows ticked under DEMO-APP, '3 of 3 selected', 'Bring back 3'.

checks.criterion: A normal close by any path shows nothing
checks.steps: Open one terminal, quit with the close button and confirm, start again; repeat with Alt+F4 and on macOS Cmd+Q.

checks.criterion: Ticked terminals reopen in order, name and pin; Claude resumes
checks.steps: From the offer above, with 'alpha' pinned, click 'Bring back 3'.
checks.expected: alpha, beta and the shell reopen in order with their names, alpha pinned, and both Claude terminals continue their conversation.

checks.criterion: A brought-back shell shows the amber line, and × removes it
checks.steps: After bringing back, look at the shell's header, then click × on the line.
checks.expected: 'Brought back after Maestro stopped. Its earlier content could not be retrieved.' on the shell only; gone after ×.

checks.criterion: A terminal whose folder is gone is greyed and cannot be ticked
checks.steps: Open a terminal in worktree C:\tmp\gone-wt, kill Maestro, delete that folder, start again.
checks.expected: A greyed, unticked row with 'folder no longer exists'.

checks.criterion: Parked terminals come back on the shelf
checks.steps: Park 'beta', kill Maestro, start again, bring all back.
checks.expected: beta on the parked shelf with the needs-you chip; nothing typed into any agent.

checks.criterion: Don't bring back, × and Esc each remove the list
checks.steps: Get the offer, press Esc, quit normally and start again; repeat with × and 'Don't bring back'.
checks.expected: The dialog closes, no terminals open, and no dialog on the next start.
